findings.title: The browser opener stays in the server's session and can open its terminal
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Start `mhfe serve`: the opener and the browser it starts run in a process group of their own but in the server's session, so /dev/tty still opens for them.
findings.expected: CORE-55: the narrowest form; the comment says they get no terminal.
findings.observed: process_group(0) keeps the session and with it the controlling terminal.
findings.impact: Where the kernel allows TIOCSTI, the browser or its opener could type into the shell after serve ends.
findings.recommendedFix: Start the opener with setsid in pre_exec, a session of its own without a controlling terminal.
findings.requiredVerification: A Linux test starts a shell through the same helper and checks that it leads its own session.

findings.title: Names shown escaped miss some invisible formatting characters
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: `escaped("/tmp/tool\u{E0041}.html")` returns the tag character as it is; U+00AD, U+180E and U+FFF9 to U+FFFB pass too.
findings.expected: Its documentation: invisible formatting characters are shown escaped.
findings.observed: Only the bidirectional controls, zero-width characters and the byte order mark are covered.
findings.impact: A file name can hide characters a person does not see.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the soft hyphen, the Mongolian vowel separator, the interlinear annotation marks and the tag characters.
findings.requiredVerification: The unit test lists U+00AD, U+FFF9 and U+E0041 among the characters not shown.

findings.title: The swap question comes before the stop for open memory
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: In a container with the host's swap on a disk and no user systemd, a secret command asks whether to go on with unencrypted swap, then stops because other programs could read its memory.
findings.expected: A command that will stop asks nothing first.
findings.observed: keep_off_swap asked before isolation and the checks at start.
findings.impact: A pointless question, answered for nothing.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep the restart before isolation, and ask after the checks at start (ask_about_swap).
findings.requiredVerification: The tool's tests and the terminal suite pass with the question after the checks.

findings.title: The swap restart starts the program by its path again
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: SECURITY.md, section Limits, at the reviewed commit: "the swap restart, and the menu on other systems, start the program by its path again".
findings.reproduction: On a system that restarts in a scope without swap, replace the file at the program's path between the start and the restart.
findings.expected: The program that runs is the one the person started, as the menu ensures on Linux.
findings.observed: systemd-run is given the program's path, so the file now at that path runs.
findings.impact: Anyone who can replace the mhfe file can run code in the next command, as SECURITY.md says already.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep the documented limit; systemd-run starts the program in a new process of the user manager, which cannot take the program's own file.
findings.requiredVerification: None: accepted as documented.

findings.title: The reproducible build's tests fail in its container since a command stops on open memory
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Blocks the release: the reproducible build or the draft would fail.
findings.evidence: Source reading; reproduced with unshare at the remediation commit.
findings.reproduction: Run the canonical build: `cargo test` in the BuildKit container runs the isolated-command test, whose child stops as secret-protection-core cannot confirm NoMemoryReading in a nested PID namespace; the test panics.
findings.expected: The canonical build passes, as before.
findings.observed: The test treats the stop as a failure of the checks at start.
findings.impact: Every tag and manual canonical build fails before any archive is made.
findings.recommendedFix: Treat a stop for open memory in the test child as the expected outcome where it happens.
findings.requiredVerification: The test passes in a new PID and user namespace (`unshare --user --pid --fork --mount-proc`) and outside one.

findings.title: The release's fuzz job checks out without the specification and cannot compile
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Blocks the release: the reproducible build or the draft would fail.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Push a tag: the fuzz job checks out without submodules, and the library's include_str of tests/spec fails to compile.
findings.expected: The job builds and runs every target.
findings.observed: The checkout lacks `submodules: true`.
findings.impact: No draft release is made, as attest needs fuzz.
findings.recommendedFix: Check out the submodule in the fuzz job.
findings.requiredVerification: The next tag's fuzz job runs; until then, the job's checkout matches the canonical job's.

findings.title: cargo xtask hardened cannot pass where System Integrity Protection is on
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: On a Mac with SIP on, the control copy of mhfe signed without the hardened runtime stops at its start, as other programs could read its memory; the check reports that it ended before the check.
findings.expected: The control waits for its input while root asks for its task port.
findings.observed: The control is a copy of mhfe, which now stops without the hardened runtime.
findings.impact: The only proof that root gets no task port of the signed program cannot be made.
findings.recommendedFix: Use a copy of /bin/cat signed ad hoc without the hardened runtime as the control.
findings.requiredVerification: A run on a Mac with SIP on, which GitHub's Macs are not.

findings.title: Intel macOS is neither tested nor linted in CI
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Read ci.yml: the portable matrix runs macOS on Apple silicon only; the release runs the Intel program's self-test and terminal suite at a tag only.
findings.expected: RUST-16: every released target runs its tests in CI.
findings.observed: No CI row for x86_64-apple-darwin.
findings.impact: The Intel program's code runs first at a tag.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a macos-15-intel row to the portable job.
findings.requiredVerification: CI's macos-15-intel job passes.

findings.title: The attestation's checksum check relies on a file from the artifact it checks
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Read release.yml: canonical.sha256 travels in the same `canonical` artifact as the archives it covers.
findings.expected: The attestation job can tell the bytes the building job made from any others.
findings.observed: Whatever replaces the artifact can replace the checksums with it.
findings.impact: A job that could replace artifacts within the run would pass the check.
findings.recommendedFix: Give the SHA-256 of the checksum file as the canonical job's output and compare it in attest.
findings.requiredVerification: The next tag's attest job passes the comparison.

findings.title: The request parser of mhfe serve has no fuzz target
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: List the fuzz targets: none reaches read_request_head, respond or split_checksum_line, which read bytes from any local process and from web pages through the browser.
findings.expected: RUST-18: every parser of untrusted input has a fuzz target.
findings.observed: The parser lives in the binary, out of the fuzz crate's reach.
findings.impact: Inputs outside the unit tests' cases are not explored.
findings.recommendedFix: Move the pure parsing to src/bin/mhfe/serve_http.rs, which the binary and a fuzz target `http` both take in.
findings.requiredVerification: The http target runs without a crash and checks every answer and its headers.

findings.title: The hidden-input line editor has no fuzz target
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: deferred, as it needs the editor moved out of the binary; the terminal suite covers its keys.
findings.evidence: TARGETS.md at the reviewed commit records it as a gap.
findings.reproduction: List the fuzz targets: none drives the line editor with keystrokes.
findings.expected: RUST-18 names input editors.
findings.observed: The editor lives in the binary and depends on its terminal and hint modules.
findings.impact: Unusual key sequences are covered by the terminal suite and unit tests only; the input comes from the person at the keyboard.
findings.recommendedFix: Give the editor a seam of its own that a fuzz target can drive.
findings.requiredVerification: A fuzz target over the editor.

findings.title: The phrases fuzz target guards its search on the wrong count
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Give `?` and one word off the list: both count as missing, and the search tries 2,048 squared candidates, seconds per input.
findings.expected: The target leaves out the two-word search, as its header says.
findings.observed: It counted only literal `?` tokens.
findings.impact: Slow inputs that waste the fuzzing budget.
findings.recommendedFix: Guard on the unreadable words of ContainerReading::read.
findings.requiredVerification: The phrases target runs at its usual speed.

findings.title: The extra refusals isolation asks for are never reported
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Read IsolationCheck: file_locks_refused, sendmsg_refused, signals_to_self_only, dynamic_code_refused and microsoft_signed_only are never read.
findings.expected: SECURITY.md: a warning names any other protection that did not take effect.
findings.observed: The warning names memory, network, file writes, threads and descriptors only.
findings.impact: A refusal the system did not apply goes unnoticed.
findings.recommendedFix: Name each option this system was asked for and did not apply.
findings.requiredVerification: The isolation check's unit test covers an option not applied on Linux and Windows.

findings.title: Small rule and test gaps in the tooling
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Read them: a comment calls Cargo.lock the one lockfile; a line of 115 columns; the Windows isolation check stopped looking for gaps that must be absent; the build context takes in the fuzz builds and corpora.
findings.expected: The coding rules and a check that proves the absence too.
findings.observed: As read.
findings.impact: Misleading comments, a slower build context, a check that would miss an extra gap.
findings.recommendedFix: Correct the comments, wrap the line, add a negative check, ignore the fuzz folders.
findings.requiredVerification: code-rules, the Windows terminal suite and a build context without fuzz/.

findings.title: The container search's comment overstates what is wiped
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Read the comment: "a container's words, packed or not, are wiped", while ContainerSearch keeps them unwiped elsewhere.
findings.expected: A comment says what the code does.
findings.observed: Only the packed bits and the working numbers are wiped.
findings.impact: A reader may rely on a wipe that does not happen; a container is not a secret under CORE-45.
findings.recommendedFix: Say what is wiped.
findings.requiredVerification: Review.

findings.title: The documents say the stack is overwritten in the browser too
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Read them against mhfe-core 06d7d00, whose stack clearing comes from secret-protection-core and writes nothing in WebAssembly.
findings.expected: The documents state the WebAssembly exception.
findings.observed: They claim the overwrite without one.
findings.impact: A reader of the browser package expects a cleared stack.
findings.recommendedFix: Say that the browser's stack stays in the worker's memory until the worker ends.
findings.requiredVerification: Review.

findings.title: The Windows message for open memory names Flatpak and user namespaces
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Read MEMORY_OPEN_TEXT: Windows gets the Linux text.
findings.expected: Advice that applies on Windows.
findings.observed: Flatpak and user namespaces on Windows.
findings.impact: Confusing advice.
findings.recommendedFix: A Windows branch: run with no debugger attached.
findings.requiredVerification: Review.

findings.title: The user documents lag the new stop and the new checks
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Read them: the README says MHFE warns, not that it stops; building from source does not say a macOS build must be signed; Windows file writes are not named; the release's fuzz job and hardened check are not named.
findings.expected: Documents that match the program.
findings.observed: As read.
findings.impact: A macOS build from source stops at every secret command with no hint in the build guide.
findings.recommendedFix: Update the four passages.
findings.requiredVerification: Review.

findings.title: The README has no contents table and no coverage record exists
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Read the README and docs/ against DOC-08 and DOC-09.
findings.expected: A contents table, and the latest measured coverage with its scope.
findings.observed: Neither.
findings.impact: Navigation, and no measured coverage for a reader.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the contents table, measure the coverage and record it in docs/COVERAGE.md with a README line.
findings.requiredVerification: The coverage record of the remediation commit.

findings.title: The generated notices' header omits Zig's compiler-rt
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: fixed with the change that touches its code.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Read the header: it names the other material described above, but not the Zig compiler-rt section.
findings.expected: The header names every section above it.
findings.observed: Zig's compiler-rt is left out.
findings.impact: A reader may miss the macOS programs' runtime notice.
findings.recommendedFix: Name it in the header and regenerate.
findings.requiredVerification: cargo xtask licences --check passes.

findings.title: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES records no reason for any direct dependency
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not release-blocking: deferred, a convention of every direct dependency that the notices generator would change at once.
findings.evidence: Source reading at the reviewed commit.
findings.reproduction: Read CORE-25 against the notices: the reasons, the new secret-protection-core's among them, are comments in Cargo.toml.
findings.expected: CORE-25: the reason of a new runtime dependency is recorded in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
findings.observed: Every direct dependency's reason is in Cargo.toml only.
findings.impact: None for the build; the reasons are one file away.
findings.recommendedFix: Generate the reasons from Cargo.toml into the notices, for every direct dependency at once.
findings.requiredVerification: cargo xtask licences writes the reasons.
